title: Job import failures all collapse to 'No valid jobs found' — corrupt file, wrong format, and empty export are indistinguishable
existing_state: JobExportService.ImportFromFile and ImportFromString wrap everything in catch-all blocks that return an empty list (Services/JobExportService.cs:71-86 and 92-107): unreadable file, malformed JSON, a non-.sshjobs JSON file, a clipboard string that isn't a GZip+Base64 export blob, and a genuinely empty export all produce the identical result. JobListDialog.ProcessImportedJobs then shows the single generic message 'No valid jobs found in the import data.' (JobListDialog.cs:1420-1427). A teammate who pastes the wrong clipboard content or picks the wrong file gets no clue whether the data was bad, the format was wrong, or the export really contained nothing — contrast with the same dialog's export path, which does surface the real exception (JobListDialog.cs:1166-1170).
recommendation: Change the two import methods to return a small result type (Jobs + ErrorKind/ErrorMessage) or throw typed exceptions caught at the call sites. Distinguish at minimum: file not found / not readable, JSON parse failure ('not a valid .sshjobs file'), decode failure ('clipboard does not contain an SSH Helper job export'), unsupported Version, and genuinely zero jobs. Surface the specific message in ProcessImportedJobs's warning dialog.
user_benefit: When sharing jobs between teammates' machines — the entire point of .sshjobs/clipboard export — a failed import tells the user what actually went wrong instead of gaslighting them about an 'empty' file.

evidence.note: catch { return new List<JobDefinition>(); } on both import paths
Single generic 'No valid jobs found in the import data.' for every failure mode
